title: Variance-aware benchmark slicer for kernel-selection and prefill-decode cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: CI perf signals are noisy; a single p99 regression often arises from coverage gaps in workload sampling. Current golden baselines rely on static seed sets and monolithic workload mixes which miss variance across model sizes, attention windows, and prefill vs decode traffic. Goal: build a variance-aware 'slicer' that partitions workload corpus into statistically coherent slices (by sequence-length distribution, attention-window histogram, prefill:decode ratio, model family) and produces slice-level golden baselines and CI gate thresholds. The slicer will feed the benchmark harness with per-slice seed locking, deterministic perturbations, and an adaptive sampling budget to surface regression signals earlier while reducing false positives.
acceptance_criteria: Slicer produces stable slices covering >=95% of production traffic volume by token distribution
Per-slice baselines produce p50/p95/p99 stability within predefined noise bands on a 7-day rolling window
CI integration: PR runs against full slicer, flags a single-slice regression if p95 increases > 10% and system-wide regression if > 5 slices fail simultaneously
End-to-end run time for the standard regression harness increases by < 20% versus today (target: ~1.2x)
Documentation and runbook for triaging slice-level regressions published in Confluence
tasks: Design slice schema and selection heuristics (sequence length buckets, attention-window quantiles, model-family tags, prefill:decode ratio)
Implement slicer service that ingests telemetry and outputs deterministic seed sets per slice
Extend benchmark orchestrator to accept slice manifests and run parallel slice jobs with per-slice kernel scoring
Add kernel-choice scoring metric that weights latency/regression risk by slice traffic importance
Integrate CI gating logic and write initial threshold rules; add alerting to perf-dashboard when slice-level regressions occur
Run broadbackfill across last 30 days of production traces to validate slice coverage and tune budgets
Write docs, runbook, and a sample RFC for runtime team review
progress_updates: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to 4 slices (short/med/long seq, decode-heavy, attention-broad vs attention-tight). Agreed to start with CPU/GPU-agnostic metrics.
2026-03-05 - Telemetry schema updated: added attention_window_percentile and prefill_decode_ratio tags. Instrumentation PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5123
2026-03-08 - Prototype slicer produced deterministic seed manifests for slices; initial runs show p99 variance reduced by ~18% for short-seq slice
2026-03-11 - CI gating proposal reviewed with SRE: thresholds for slice-level p95 increase set to 10%; gating logic will include hysteresis window of 3 runs to avoid flapping
review_feedback: PM review (Lena Ortiz): prefer conservative gate (fewer false positives); recommended we include a lightweight synthetic jitter generator to stress decode scheduling paths
Design review (Evan Kim): suggested visual drilldown in Console that overlays kernel-selection heatmap on top of slice timelines
SRE review (Priya Nair): asked for runbook steps for rollback and temporary kernel fallback when slice-triggered regressions affect production SLAs
decisions: MVP slices chosen: short (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), long (>512), decode-heavy (>70% decode tokens)
Use seed locking with deterministic RNG salted by slice id to permit reproducible fuzz runs
Kernel scoring will be additive: baseline latency penalty + attention-window penalty + historical instability multiplier
CI gate semantics: failing a single critical slice will create a 'must-fix' signal; fail across multiple slices escalates to a blocked release
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: explosion of slices leads to long CI runs. Mitigation: adaptive sampling budget and prioritization; start with 4 slices and allow dynamic merging
Risk: telemetry tags are incomplete for older models. Mitigation: backfill heuristics using token-length proxies and conservative default slices
Risk: false positives from noisy infra. Mitigation: require 3-run hysteresis and correlate with infra-level metrics (GPU thermal throttling, rack-level issues) before gating
test_plan: Backfill run across 30 days of production traces to validate slice coverage and estimate noise bands
A/B: run new slicer in shadow against current golden baseline for two weeks and compare alert rates
Smoke test: introduce synthetic attention-window stress and verify slice-level detection and kernel fallback behavior
CI integration test: run sample PR that deliberately changes kernel routing heuristic and ensure gate trips on expected slice
release_notes: Introduce variance-aware workload slicing to improve detection of kernel-selection regressions
Add slice-level baselines and CI gating to reduce noisy global gating and speed triage
Expose slice heatmaps in Console for triage and kernel scoring visualization
